But the long Team B name has the bottoms of its 'g' and 'y' cut off in every long-value frame, and that alone keeps it off air. basicMistakes.where: Long Team B name 'Åbo Akademi Gaming Society', right side of the bug: the field mask cuts off the descenders of 'g' in 'Gaming' and 'y' in 'Society' at the baseline, and the ring of the Å is clipped at the top

All five operator actions are there. But the long Team B name has its descenders (and the ring of the Å) cut off by the field mask, which is a basic clipping mistake in the stress frames. The long Team A name is shrunk and sits higher than Team B, so the two sides look mismatched, and the crests sit on grey plates of their own. Next map does not visibly advance the map either. resume (button exists, but it returns the bug to pre-match instead of live)

otherProblems: After the reveal the kicker still reads 'AND THE NOMINEES ARE'. Nothing on the board says 'winner'; only the gold tile shows who won.
In the long-value frames (G-5/6/7) the director name is the large line and the film title is the small caps line. In the sample frames it is the other way round, so the hierarchy is inconsistent.
With empty values (G-8/9/10) the board is a large black box holding only the category title, with a lot of dead space. Operators would not normally put it on air in that state.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, centred black-and-gold board. It has a gold hairline frame, a category title with a short gold rule underneath, and four equal nominee tiles in a 2x2 grid. All text is cream or gold on near-black, so it stays readable over the grey, light and busy grounds. Long category names and director names fit without clipping: the names wrap neatly inside their tiles, and the panel grows to hold them. The native crops are crisp. Suspense dims the nominees and gives the board a slight push-in. Reveal lights the winner's tile in gold with dark text and dims the others, which still stay legible. Take and Out are clean fades. Both required operator actions are there and work. The flaws are minor wording and hierarchy issues that viewers would barely notice.

otherProblems: The long username breaks mid-word with no hyphen ('xX_Ångström_Gänseblümc' / 'hen_Xx') in G-5, G-6 and G-7. Nothing is clipped, but it reads less cleanly than an ellipsis would.

A faint dark-green rule at the panel's bottom right sits just under the end of the message ('at…' in the long frames, 'stream!' in the sample). It is barely visible and reads as stray furniture rather than a deliberate timer bar.
With empty values (G-8 to G-10) the panel stays full size with only 'NEW DONATION' in it, which leaves a large empty dark area.
With the sample values no amount is shown (anonymous donation), so the amount only appears in the long-value frames.
answer.reasons: G would air. It's a clean dark card at the top right with a green accent bar, an avatar ring, a monospace 'NEW DONATION' label, a bold name, a lighter message and a right-aligned amount. The text is legible over the video, light and busy backgrounds. The white shield avatar is clearly visible on its dark circle, and the long message ends in a clean ellipsis inside its field. Hold keeps the alert on screen, Resume lets the timer take it off, Replay rebuilds it and Skip clears it, so the operator has everything the brief asks for. The weak spots are the unhyphenated mid-word break in the long username and a faint stray rule near the message's last line. A designer would tidy those, but a viewer would hardly notice them and nothing is clipped, overlapping or unreadable.

otherProblems: The long username wraps mid-word ('Gänseblümc / hen_Xx') with no hyphen (G-5, G-6, G-7). It stays inside the panel but reads a little awkwardly.
The thin teal timer hairline at the bottom right of the panel is faint and could pass for a stray rule.
With empty values the panel shows only the 'NEW DONATION' kicker next to a large empty area (G-8 to G-10). This is acceptable as a fallback, but it looks sparse.
answer.reasons: This airs. It's a clean dark alert panel in the top right with a green accent bar, a circular avatar well and a clear hierarchy: kicker, then name, then message, with the amount on the top right. It stays readable over the video, light and busy grounds. The stress values wrap the name onto two lines and cut the message off with a clean ellipsis, all inside the panel. The white avatar shows up well on the dark circle and the amount lines up with the kicker. Hold keeps the alert on screen, Resume and Skip clear it, and Replay brings it back. The panel animates in and out cleanly. The only flaws are small ones a viewer would barely notice: the name breaks mid-word, and the timer hairline is faint.

otherProblems: The long username breaks mid-word with no hyphen ('…Gänseblümc / hen_Xx') in G-5, G-6 and G-7. Nothing is clipped, but a designer would rather see a cleaner break or a reduced size.
The sample-value frames (G-2 to G-4) show no amount at all, while the long-value frames show €25.00 at the top right. The frames don't make clear whether the sample simply had no amount.
The thin green timer line at the bottom right of the panel is very faint and short, and it looks the same length at 20 ms, 1500 ms and 10000 ms. It reads more like a stray stroke than a progress bar.
With empty values (G-8 to G-10) the panel keeps its full width and shows only 'NEW DONATION', which leaves a lot of empty dark plate.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, dark top-right alert with a green accent bar and a ringed avatar. The type is clear and readable over video, light and busy backgrounds. The white avatar sits safely on a dark disc with a green ring. Long umlaut names and the long message stay inside the panel, and the message ends in a clean ellipsis. Hold, resume, replay and skip are all offered and visibly work: hold keeps the alert up at 10 s, resume and skip clear it, and replay builds it again. Nothing overlaps, gets clipped or escapes the panel. The remaining issues are small: the username breaks mid-word, the sample frames show no amount, and the timer line is faint.

otherProblems: Suspense is a very subtle change: all four nominees dim slightly and the grid eases in a little, so a viewer may hardly notice it.
After the reveal the kicker still reads 'AND THE NOMINEES ARE'; it never changes to a winner line.
On the stress values the two-line hyphenated names ('Okonkwo-/Fitzgerald') make those cards taller and busier than the one-line cards beside them.
With the long category the gap between the title and the gold rule grows, and the rule is narrower than the title above it.
answer.reasons: This graphic airs as delivered. It is a clean, centred black-and-gold board with even padding, a balanced 2×2 grid of nominees, and strong cream-on-black type that stays readable over the light, busy and video backgrounds. That matters with a bright LED wall behind it. The long category name fits on one line, and the long names wrap cleanly inside their cards with no clipping or collisions. The board offers both actions the brief asks for, suspense and reveal, and the reveal gives the winner a clear gold card while the other nominees dim but stay readable. The only problems are small ones a viewer would barely notice, such as how subtle the suspense change is and the kicker staying the same after the reveal.

otherProblems: After the reveal the kicker still reads 'AND THE NOMINEES ARE' and nothing labels the gold tile as the winner. The highlight carries the moment on its own.

With long values the tiles show the director as the main line and the film as the sub-line, the reverse of the sample layout. Because names wrap at their hyphens, the top row is also taller than the bottom row (G-5 to G-7).
In the long-value state there is a slightly loose gap between the category title and the gold rule (G-5).
answer.reasons: This is a clean, centred black-and-gold board with a clear hierarchy: a gold kicker, a big category title, a centred rule and four equal tiles. The opaque dark plate keeps every line readable over the light, busy and video grounds. Long names wrap neatly at their hyphens inside the tiles, and the long category fits on one line. Nothing is clipped and nothing collides. Suspense dims the nominees evenly, and the reveal turns the winner's tile a solid gold with dark text while the other three dim but stay readable. That gives a clear payoff for the cue. Take and Out are clean fades. The remaining issues are small details a viewer would hardly notice, so it airs as delivered.

basicMistakes.where: Interval state: the header only turns a slightly deeper blue and the clock dims. No intermission label (e.g. PŘESTÁVKA) appears anywhere, so the intermission the operator calls never shows on screen.
Final state: the header turns navy but still reads '1. TŘETINA 20:00'. No final or KONEC label appears, so the result is never shown as final.

otherProblems: Both crests sit on light-blue circular plates of their own (G-4, G-86, G-87) rather than standing on the panel.

The goals-per-period table is pushed to the far right of a wide bottom band that is otherwise empty (G-2, G-4). With a single period column (G-2, G-23) about 80% of that band holds nothing, so it reads as unfinished.
With empty values (G-6) the period header is blank and the whole bottom third of the panel is empty, so the board looks broken.
answer.reasons: G would not go on air as delivered. Text handling is good: the long Czech names with diacritics fit cleanly, the score and clock are large and readable on both grounds, and the take and out animations are clean. But the intermission and final calls only show up as a subtle change of header colour, with no word to tell viewers the game is in intermission or over. That fails two of the five operator actions the brief needs. On top of that, the crests sit on their own blue disc plates, and the period breakdown sits in one corner of a mostly empty bottom band, which makes the panel look lopsided.

otherProblems: The long Team A name wraps to two lines (G-4, G-8, G-66 to G-70), so the top row is taller than the bottom one. The strip still stays balanced and contained.
End Set was pressed at 0:0, so no frame shows a set actually being awarded and the points being zeroed. Nothing visibly breaks, but the behaviour cannot be confirmed from these frames.
Partway through the Take (G-13) the panel is briefly semi-transparent, and the bottom PKT box shifts slightly past the panel edge. Both clear by 300 ms.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, compact navy strip in the top-right corner. It has a thin yellow top rule, SETY/PKT column headers, and the current-set points in strong yellow boxes. White names stay readable over both the video and light grounds. Polish letters render correctly: ó, Ś, ę, Ł. The longest name wraps neatly to two lines inside its field without clipping, and the serve dot sits well clear of the text. Point A and Point B each add the point and move the dot to that team. Undo reverses the point. Final swaps to a tidy sets-only layout with a KONIEC MECZU bar, and Out is clean. No text collides, contrast is good throughout, and nothing escapes the panel once settled. A director would put it on air as delivered.

basicMistakes.where: Interval state: the header still reads '1. TŘETINA' and only the band turns a slightly darker blue and the clock greys out. No intermission label ever appears, so the intermission the operator calls is not visible on air.
Full time state: the header turns navy but still reads '1. TŘETINA 20:00'. No 'KONEC' or final label appears, so the final is never shown to the viewer.

otherProblems: Goals-per-period block (G-2, G-8, G-41 and others): a single small column ('1', 0, 0) is pushed into the bottom-right corner, leaving roughly a third of the panel as empty white space. The panel looks unfinished.
Period header digits are tiny next to the scores, and the label '1' in the sample frames has no dot while the long-values frames show '1.'. The labelling is inconsistent.
Both crests sit on light-blue disc plates of their own (G-86.png, G-87.png). The white-and-gold crest nearly disappears against the pale disc.
With empty values (G-6) the clock turns red at 0:00 and the period label is blank, so the header is half empty.
answer.reasons: G would not go on air as delivered. The board itself is clean and readable. The long Czech names with diacritics fit without clipping, and the clock starts, stops and resets correctly. But the brief needs the operator to call the intermission and the final, and neither call shows anything a viewer can read. The header keeps saying '1. TŘETINA' and only its tint changes. The period breakdown also sits in one corner of a mostly empty bottom panel, and the crests are put on pale discs that swallow the white crest. Those are design faults a director would send back.

otherProblems: Both crests sit on their own light-blue circular plates (G-4, G-86, G-87). The white-and-gold crest on that pale disc has weak contrast and reads as a placeholder badge, not a club crest.

The goals-per-period band takes about a third of the panel's height. In the main sample state (G-2, G-3, and the other sample-value frames from G-16 on) it holds only one tiny column ('1 / 0 / 0') pushed into the bottom-right corner. The rest of the band is empty, so the panel looks unfinished. Even with three periods (G-4) the left half of the band is still empty.
The period-breakdown numbers and headers are small compared with the rest of the board and hard to read at TV distance.
Interval (G-40, G-41) only tints the header and greys the clock. There is no intermission label, so a viewer cannot tell the game is in a break.
Final (G-52, G-53) only turns the header navy. It still reads '1. TŘETINA 20:00' with no 'final' label, so the final result is never clearly shown.
With empty values (G-6, G-7) the header shows a red 0:00 with nothing on the left, and the whole breakdown band is blank.
answer.reasons: There are no basic mistakes. Long Czech names with diacritics fit cleanly, nothing overlaps or gets clipped, the clock runs, and every required operator action exists. It still would not air as delivered. Each crest sits on its own pale-blue disc, which is a logo-on-a-plate problem. The large period-breakdown band at the bottom is mostly empty, with one small column jammed into the corner, so the panel looks broken. Interval and final barely change what the viewer sees: there is no intermission or final label, and the final state still says 1st period 20:00. A designer would want the crest plates and the bottom band redesigned, and clear interval and final states, before putting it on air.

otherProblems: When a long name wraps to two lines (G-4, G-8), the top row gets taller than the bottom one. The rhythm is a little uneven but still tidy.
During the Take (G-14, 300 ms) the second row's score cells sit briefly offset to the right of the first row's. This lasts a single frame, and the board is settled by 600 ms.
End set was only pressed at 0–0, so no frame shows a set being awarded to the leading team. Nothing looked wrong; that behaviour just isn't shown.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, compact navy strip in the top-right corner with a thin yellow top rule, clear SETY/PKT headers, grey set cells and bold yellow point cells, and it reads well over both the dark and the light backgrounds. Long Polish names with ę and Ł wrap neatly inside the panel with no clipping. The serve dot sits correctly in front of the serving team and moves with Point A and Point B. Undo, the end-set reset and New match all leave a tidy board. The final look swaps PKT for a well-balanced KONIEC MECZU bar. Every action the brief asks for is on the operator surface, and no frame shows text over text, clipping or a contrast problem.

otherProblems: Long team names wrap onto two lines rather than shrinking or using an ellipsis. They stay inside the panel and are readable, but row A becomes taller than row B.
The serve dot sits in the narrow left padding, close to the panel edge. It reads clearly but the padding is tight.
In the Take, at 300 ms (G-14), team B's PKT box briefly overshoots the panel edge by a few pixels. It is gone once the graphic settles.
answer.reasons: This is a compact, clean navy strip in the top-right with a thin yellow top accent. It has clear SETY/PKT headers and a strong yellow points box, and it reads well over both the video and light backgrounds. The long Polish names with diacritics (Częstochowianka, Łódzki) render fully inside the panel. Point A and Point B add the point and move the serve dot to the scoring team. Undo, serve, end-set and new-match all leave the board settled and intact. The final look (sets only, plus a KONIEC MECZU band) is tidy and balanced. Every operator action the brief needs is on the surface. No frame has overlaps, clipping or contrast problems; the only flaws are a minor padding nit and a split-second animation overshoot.

otherProblems: The panel keeps a fixed height. With the five-row long-values field (G-5/6/7), about 150 px of empty black is left under the last row, so the bottom of the tower looks unfilled.
When the Session title is updated to its long value (G-41–45), all the competitor names and gaps shrink to a smaller size, which a viewer would notice as the rows jumping.
The gap column ends about 85 px before the panel's right edge, while the DNF badge sits flush to that edge, so the right-hand column does not line up.
In the long-values frames, a stray grey dash sits next to the DNF badge. It does not appear in the sample state.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, readable timing tower down the left side of the frame. White condensed type on a dark panel holds up on the light, busy and video grounds. The Norwegian letters (Ø, Å, Æ) render correctly, and the longest double-barrelled names fit without clipping. The DNF row is clearly dimmed and badged. Focus highlights one row and dims the rest, Whole field brings the full board back, and Final adds a clear "· FINAL" tag. Take and Out are clean. The problems are polish: the fixed-height panel leaves dead space when there are fewer rows, the rows shrink when the title is updated, and the gap column and DNF badge end at different points on the right. None of these is a basic mistake, and none makes the board unreadable.

otherProblems: In the long-value frames (G-5/6/7) the panel keeps its full height with only five rows, so about the bottom quarter of the tower is empty dark plate.
When the session title is updated (G-41 to G-45), every row's name and gap text shrinks noticeably, so the board visibly changes size because of a title change.
The gap column ends at about x=770, but the DNF badge runs to the panel's right edge at x=856. The two right-hand columns don't line up, which leaves a dead strip to the right of the gaps.
In the long frames the DNF row shows a stray '–' dash next to the DNF badge.
In the focus state the DNF row is no longer dimmed differently from the other unfocused rows, so its status cue gets weaker.
answer.reasons: I'd put this tower on air as delivered. It's a clean, high-contrast tower down the left side, and the Norwegian letters (Ø, Å, Æ) and double-barrelled names all fit in their rows, including the stress names. The DNF entry is handled clearly. Focus highlights one row with a lit band and dims the others, Whole field brings the full list back, and Final adds a blue 'FINAL' tag and darkens the position boxes for places 2 to 7. Nothing overlaps, gets clipped or is hard to read on the video, light or busy backgrounds. What remains are layout nits: empty space below short fields, the gap column not lining up with the DNF badge, and row text shrinking when the title is updated. A viewer might notice them, but none of them make the tower unairable.

otherProblems: The panel height is fixed. With the five-row stress field (G-5, G-6, G-7) a dark empty block about 150 px tall sits under the last row, so the tower reads as half-filled instead of sized to its content.

The gap column is right-aligned at about x=770, but the DNF badge and the blue header rule run to about x=856. This leaves a dead strip right of every gap and puts the times and the DNF badge on different right edges.
A flat grey band about 10 px tall runs along the whole bottom edge of the panel. On the light ground (G-3, G-6, G-9) it reads as a stray plate rather than a shadow or a designed accent.
Updating Session to its long value (G-41 to G-45) also shrinks the name and gap type in every row. The board visibly changes scale when only the header changed.
answer.reasons: I would not put this tower on air as delivered, though nothing in it is a basic mistake. Text never collides, clips or loses contrast on any background, the long Norwegian names with Æ, Ø and Å fit without truncation, and the DNF row is clearly marked. The focus, whole-field and final actions all work cleanly, and the operator surface offers all three. What keeps it off air is the desk-level finish. The fixed-height panel leaves a large empty block under a shorter field, the gap times don't share a right edge with the DNF badge and the header rule, and a grey strip under the panel looks like an accident on a light picture. The type also rescales when the session title is updated. Each is small, but together a viewer would see an unbalanced board, so it needs another pass first.

basicMistakes.where: Answer grid after Select answer: nothing changes. No answer is highlighted or marked as picked, so the select step leaves the board looking the same as before it.
Answer grid after Lock it in, then Reveal choice: only the 'ANSWER LOCKED' tag is visible. The reveal never shows which letter the captain picked.
Reveal correct state: only the correct answer (B) is highlighted. No frame anywhere shows the team's pick, so the brief's 'reveal the pick' step never appears on screen.

missingActions: revealChoice / select: the captain's pick is never shown in any frame. Select changes nothing on screen, and Reveal choice after Lock changes nothing either.
otherProblems: Single-line answers sit at the top of their white cells while the A–D letter tabs are vertically centred. This leaves the bottom half of each cell empty and the cells look misaligned (G-4, G-8, G-10, crops G-64 to G-67).
With a two-line question there is a large dead band of green between the question and the answer grid (G-4, G-51).
In the judged state the wrong answers are dimmed to pale grey-green on white, and their tabs to white letters on pale mint. Both are low contrast and will wash out on a projector (G-40).
The 'ANSWER LOCKED' tag sits on top of the white top rule and cuts through it. It reads as stuck on rather than built into the board (G-28).
answer.reasons: The board itself is clean: bold green and white, large readable type, long questions and answers wrap without clipping, and the Take, Out and correct-answer reveal all work. But the brief depends on showing the captain's pick. Select changes nothing on screen, and Reveal choice after Lock shows only the 'ANSWER LOCKED' tag, never a letter. No frame ever shows the team's choice, so neither the secret-pick sequence nor the plain select–lock–reveal sequence works as asked. On top of that, single-line answers sit at the top of half-empty cells next to centred letter tabs, and the dimmed wrong answers in the judged state are too faint for a projector. It cannot air as delivered.

otherProblems: G-4/G-5 (long values): single-line answers ('Hugo Alvar Henrik Aalto', 'Aino Marsio-Aalto', 'Eliel Saarinen…') hug the top of tall white tiles and leave the lower half empty, while the A–D letters stay vertically centred. Text and letter no longer line up, and the tiles read as broken.
G-4: 'Lars Sonck' in tile C sits lower than the single-line answers in B and D. The vertical alignment of answer text changes from tile to tile (see crops G-64 to G-67).
G-4/G-5: a short question leaves an empty dark-green band between the question and the answer grid, so the panel looks unevenly padded.
G-18 to G-23: 'Select answer' makes no visible change on the board, so the plain select → lock → reveal path shows the viewer nothing when the answer is selected.
G-57 to G-62: 'Reveal choice' after 'Lock it in' changes nothing; the board stays as it was. No frame ever shows the captain's pick on its own.
G-24 to G-29: the 'ANSWER LOCKED' tab straddles the white top rule. It looks bolted onto the edge rather than part of the panel.
G-40 and later: on the correct-answer reveal, the dimmed wrong answers (grey-green text, and white letters on pale mint tiles) are low-contrast and may wash out on a projector.
answer.reasons: With the sample values the board is clean: bold green and white, large readable question and answer text, a clear correct-answer reveal, and no clipping or collisions in any frame. The stress values expose a layout fault, though. Short answers stick to the top of tall tiles while the letters stay centred, the text sits at different heights from tile to tile, and an empty band opens under a shorter question. A viewer will see that as broken alignment. On top of that, 'Select' gives no visible feedback, and 'Reveal choice' never shows a pick in any frame. That leaves the secret-pick workflow in the brief unproven. It is close, but it needs fixes before it can air.

otherProblems: With long values (G-4, G-5, G-8 to G-11, crops G-64 to G-67), short answers sit top-left in tall white boxes while the A–D letter tiles are centred. The text sits in one corner of mostly empty boxes and doesn't line up with its letter. C and D text also start at different heights.

Select answer (G-18 to G-23) makes no visible change, and Reveal choice after the lock (G-57 to G-62) reveals nothing. No frame ever shows the team captain's pick that the brief's secret-pick and plain-select flows depend on.
The 'ANSWER LOCKED' tag (G-24 to G-29) sits on the white top rule, and the rule runs into it, which reads as clumsy.
A two-line question leaves a dead green gap above the answer grid (G-4, G-47 to G-51).
The dimmed wrong answers in the judge state are pale grey-green on white, readable but weak on a projector.
answer.reasons: The sample state is clean, bold green and white, readable, and the correct-answer reveal works.
